instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of "lobbyist" covers any individual employed by a principal or who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal" with no dollar threshold, so any compensation triggers lobbyist status.

The "lobbyist" definition in §13.62(11) contains no expenditure-based standard; the $500 threshold in §13.64(1) is a principal-side registration trigger, not a lobbyist-side expenditure threshold, so no statute defines a lobbyist-side expenditure standard.

Section 13.68(1)(a)6. requires itemized listing of the lobbyist's name, address, and total amount only if expenditures/obligations to that lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period, establishing a $200 per-lobbyist itemization threshold.

Section 13.621(5) allows a principal anticipating not more than $500 in aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations in a calendar year to file a simple verified statement in lieu of licensing under §13.63, registration under §13.64, and reporting under §13.68; §13.64(1) likewise requires registration only when expenditures exceed $500.

Wisconsin's lobbyist definition uses a "5 days" of lobbying communications standard, not a percentage of compensated time, and no other provision in §§13.61–13.695 establishes a time-percent de minimis exemption from filing.

content.text:
I'll analyze each row against the Wisconsin statute text.

**row_001 (compensation threshold for lobbyist definition):** §13.62(11) defines "lobbyist" as someone who "is employed by a principal, or contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal" — no dollar threshold.

**row_002 (lobbyist-side expenditure threshold):** No such statute exists in Wisconsin. The $500 threshold in §13.64(1) is a principal-side registration trigger, not a lobbyist-side expenditure threshold.

**row_003 (time standard for lobbyist definition):** §13.62(11) — if duties aren't exclusively lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist only if they make lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period.

**row_004 (per-item itemization threshold):** §13.68(1)(a)6. requires listing a lobbyist by name only if expenditures to that lobbyist exceed $200 in the reporting period. There's also §13.68(1)(a)5. ($500 for paid advertising aggregate). The closest per-item itemization threshold is $200.

**row_005 (de minimis filing exemption):** §13.621(5) — principals anticipating not more than $500 aggregate in a calendar year can file a verified statement and are exempt from registration/reporting under §§13.63, 13.64, 13.68.

**row_006 (time-percent filing exemption):** Wisconsin uses a "5 days" rule, not a percentage. No percent-of-compensated-time threshold for the lobbyist's own filing exemption exists.

input.justification: The definition of "lobbyist" covers any individual employed by a principal or who "contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal" with no dollar threshold, so any compensation triggers lobbyist status.

The "lobbyist" definition in §13.62(11) contains no expenditure-based standard; the $500 threshold in §13.64(1) is a principal-side registration trigger, not a lobbyist-side expenditure threshold, so no statute defines a lobbyist-side expenditure standard.

Section 13.62(11) provides that if an individual's duties are not exclusively lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist only if he or she makes lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period.

Section 13.68(1)(a)6. requires itemized listing of the lobbyist's name, address, and total amount only if expenditures/obligations to that lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period, establishing a $200 per-lobbyist itemization threshold.

Section 13.621(5) allows a principal anticipating not more than $500 in aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations in a calendar year to file a simple verified statement in lieu of licensing under §13.63, registration under §13.64, and reporting under §13.68; §13.64(1) likewise requires registration only when expenditures exceed $500.

Wisconsin's lobbyist definition uses a "5 days" of lobbying communications standard, not a percentage of compensated time, and no other provision in §§13.61–13.695 establishes a time-percent de minimis exemption from filing.
